title: Memory telemetry ledger and proactive headroom policy for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a memory telemetry ledger and a proactive headroom reservation policy that budgets GPU memory across model weights, KV cache, and activations. Provide runtime sensors, a lightweight on-node ledger, and a controller policy to convert observed tail usage into soft reserves that prevent OOMs while minimizing reserved capacity overhead. Deliverables: on-node telemetry schema, ledger write/read API, headroom policy algorithm, simulation harness results, e2e integration test, and rollout plan with metrics and dashboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Node telemetry emits structured memory samples (weights, kv_bytes, activations_peak, slab_usage) at 1s and 10s windows
Ledger aggregates 1h/6h/24h peak estimates and exposes projected headroom recommendation API
Headroom policy reduces simulated OOM rate by >= 80% for heavy-KV workloads in the simulator
Memory reserved by soft-headroom increases average GPU utilization by <= 4% (cost overhead) in synthetic workloads
E2E smoke test validates fallback: if soft reserve cannot be satisfied, requests are routed to model-variant with lower KV footprint
Documentation, runbook, and console dashboard for the ledger published
tasks: Finalize telemetry schema and sampling cadence
Implement on-node ledger (C++) with ring-buffer persistence
Create aggregator service that computes sliding-window peak estimator
Prototype headroom policy in the autoscaler (k8s operator hook)
Run 3 bucketed simulations (chatty, long-context, mixed) and record OOMs/latency/cost
Add dashboard panels and alerting for projected headroom and reserve utilization
Prepare rollout gating and canary criteria
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — scoped features and success criteria with PM/Product (Marisol). Decided to use dual-window estimator (short 10s, long 1h) to balance spikes vs sustained growth.

2026-03-11: Telemetry schema proposal posted: weight_mb, kv_bytes, activations_peak_bytes, slab_frag, reserved_soft, reserved_hard. Link: https://app.confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Memory+Telemetry+Ledger
2026-03-11: Spike results — microbenchmarks show 0.6% CPU overhead for 1s sampling; acceptable for on-node probe. See spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleTelemetrySpike

2026-03-12: Implemented prototype ledger write API and ring-buffer format. Initial aggregator script computes P95/P99 peaks; current integration test simulates 500 tenants and reports 12% lower OOMs vs baseline when applying naive static reserve.

2026-03-13: Design review with SRE and Runtime leads. Feedback: make headroom 'soft' by allowing reclaim under pressure and require fallbacks to model-variant instead of preempting KV for tenant isolation. Action: add reclaim priority tiers and model-variant fallback policy. Linked GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6821
2026-03-13: Updated acceptance criteria to require <=4% cost overhead and >=80% OOM reduction in simulator. Added canary plan to only enable soft-reserve for P1 customers initially.
risks: Over-reserving memory will reduce overall cluster throughput and increase cost for customers if policy is too conservative
Telemetry sampling could add jitter that interferes with tight latency SLOs if cadence is too aggressive
Reclaim rules that evict KV may degrade quality for chat sessions (risk to customer experience)
Interplay with Dedicated capacity autoscaler requires coordination to avoid double-reserving
decisions: Adopt dual-window (10s short, 1h long) sliding peak estimator instead of exponential EWMA to better capture bursty long-context scenarios
Implement soft-reserve that is reclaimable under pressure; hard-reserve only for reserved capacity customers
Prefer model-variant fallback over KV eviction when per-tenant QoS is high priority
Persist ledger as compact ring-buffer to minimize on-node storage and allow crash recovery
next_steps: Add reclaim priority tiers and implement model-variant routing hook
Run full produced workload simulation and log cost/loss metrics
Prepare canary rollout on dedicated pool with A/B comparison and dashboarding
